question: What are pre-trained models for NLP, how can they be categorised, and how are they adapted to downstream tasks?
contributions: Comprehensive review of PTMs for NLP
New taxonomy from four perspectives: representation type, architecture, pre-training task, extensions
Collection of resources (implementations, corpora, paper lists)
Discussion of limitations and future directions

limits: Survey: no experiments of its own; numbers are compiled from original papers and mixed metrics (Table 3 notes MiniLM QQP accuracy incomparable).
Covers up to early 2021 (prefix/prompt tuning, GPT-3 briefly); predates instruction tuning and RLHF-era LLMs.
Authors concede PTMs cannot handle >512 tokens, fine-tuning is brittle across seeds, and interpretability via attention is controversial.
practices: Choose a PTM whose pre-training task, architecture and corpus match the target task and data distribution (5.2.1).
Use top-layer representation for simple transfer, or an ELMo-style softmax-weighted sum of all layers (5.2.2).
Prefer fine-tuning over feature extraction as more general and convenient (5.2.3).
Use two-stage fine-tuning (further pre-training on in-domain corpus or intermediate supervised task) to improve BERT (5.3).
Use adapters/PALs to avoid per-task copies of parameters (5.3).
Use gradual or sequential unfreezing when fine-tuning (5.3).
Compress PTMs by pruning, quantization, parameter sharing, distillation, module replacing or early exit for deployment (4.5).
